note: City of Barnum campground on Bear Lake, right beside I-35 between Duluth and Moose Lake. Tent sites as well as RV sites; swim beach (no lifeguard), playground, nature trail and easy access to the public boat landing. Canoe rentals. Weekly, monthly and seasonal stays are sold alongside nights. --Claude
summary: City page + 2026 brochure read: daily RV $50 (tent $40; weekly $300, monthly $800, seasonal $1,800), open May 15-Oct 1 (now manual), electric+water at RV sites, dump, showers; fees due on arrival; no site count or amperage. Lakeview kept. Google 4.2/45. Seasonal share could not be measured.
flags: LONG-STAY check (city-run, mostly-seasonal question unresolved): the city sells 'seasonal, monthly, weekly and daily rates' (seasonal RV $1,800, monthly $800) and posts a daily RV rate of $50. No site count or seasonal/nightly split is published. Summer imagery shows about a dozen similar trailers lined up along the east row by the shore and a few units on the west side of the loop, which looks like seasonal occupancy, but that is not measurable from a photo. Google Maps (as 'Bear Lake Park Campground') 4.2 from 45 reviews; the visible reviews describe overnight stays ('Had a waterfront site. One of the nicest places we stopped so far', 9 years ago; 'Small, hidden place ... noise from the nearby Interstate ... Many of the sites are small and tight, and require a sharp downhill ...', 7 years ago). Booking is by phone to the campground host. Read as possibly seasonal-heavy but with a posted nightly rate and recent transient reviews; not called a drop candidate, reviewer to judge.
Price: $50 daily RV is high for a city campground, but the price gate applies to private parks only.
Rig fit: a 2018-era Google review says 'Many of the sites are small and tight, and require a sharp downhill' (rest truncated); the city states no length limit. No change.

Waterfront: lakeview kept. The RV row along the east side of the loop (about 46.4990,-92.6812 to 46.4983,-92.6810) sits 15-30 m from Bear Lake behind a band of shoreline trees and marsh, with a dock at the south end; no site has open ground to the water on current imagery (an older aerial in the city brochure shows fewer trees). A 9-year-old review says 'Had a waterfront site': a lead only.
Hookups: electric at the RV sites is stated without amperage, so electric is not written; a review says 'No sewer hookups' (not an operator source; nothing written).
